## TL;DR

Task #1108 adds bounded automatic recovery for failed review runs and for overdue engineer messages, with separate configurable controls, visible activity, and protections for tasks deliberately held, paused, or assigned to a human. Review round 1 also exposed shared retry state between failed-report retries and timeout retries. That state has now been split: `review_failed_report_retries` is persisted independently from `review_timeout_retries`, and a regression test covers both event orderings. The handoff check repeatedly failed on a remote host lock timeout test, although that test passed in isolation locally. Its two-second fixed sleep has been replaced by a test-controlled release marker so the holder stays live until the waiter has observed the occupied slot.

## Work and rationale

The original behavior treated a reviewer process that exited without a usable report as a task needing human input. That conflated an agent execution failure with an actual review verdict. The implementation recognizes the no-output failure path separately, schedules a bounded retry, writes an activity marker for each automatic attempt, and explains the exhausted retry reason when it can no longer continue. The bound is configurable under `review.failedReportRetries` and defaults to two retries.

A previous implementation reused `review_timeout_retries` for both hard review timeouts and no-output failures. This made the two recovery budgets interfere: spending a timeout retry could reduce the remaining no-output attempts, and conversely a failed-report run could prevent the independent timeout retry. The fix introduces a distinct `review_failed_report_retries` frontmatter value and in-memory manager counter. It is persisted before the timer fires, so a server restart does not replenish the budget. A successful or incomplete report clears each episode's relevant counters. The test exercises timeout followed by no-output and no-output followed by timeout, asserting the two counts do not consume one another.

The second recovery path addresses a task that has been returned for fixes while the engineer message remains queued. The watchdog uses a configurable queued-message age threshold (three minutes by default), requires there to be no live engineer, and restarts work on the task's existing worktree. Held, paused, human-assigned, and pressure-guarded tasks are excluded. Recovery and retry activity are recorded so the board timeline explains the action. The Settings UI, config schema, supported TOML key list, and user and operator documentation were updated together; tests cover configuration and the exclusion conditions.

## Approaches tried

For the retry-counter bug, I followed the no-output and timeout paths from `ReviewManager` through the durable task metadata helpers. Keeping one shared counter with adjusted increment logic was not sufficient because each retry policy has a distinct cap and lifecycle. The implementation therefore uses separate persisted keys and separate in-memory maps, while retaining independent reset behavior.

For the remote lock test failure, I first reproduced the named test locally using the same focused Vitest invocation. It passed, which suggested a scheduling-sensitive test rather than a deterministic functional failure. The existing test waited for the holder to write a start marker, then relied on a fixed two-second sleep to keep the lock occupied while a zero-wait caller ran. Under a loaded remote runner, process scheduling and orchestration time could consume that fixed interval. The test now has the holder poll for a release file. The test creates that file only after the waiter command has returned, so the holder cannot vacate its slot before the timeout is observed. A `finally` block releases the holder even when the waiter command throws.

## Challenges and blockers

The full scoped check had failed more than once on the remote `remote-host-pool.test.ts` lock test even though a local isolated run passed. The failure was reported as a remote validation test failure, so local test success alone was not enough to hand off. The synchronization change specifically removes the timing assumption implicated by the failure; the requested scoped gate still needs to pass on the final tree.

One reviewer noted an edge case where an overdue queued engineer message may exist while a task is still in `review`, whereas the no-engineer recovery scan currently covers `active`. The provided report described this as an edge case and made extending the scan conditional on confirmation that this state occurs in production. I did not broaden the watchdog based only on speculation; recovery eligibility for this state remains an item for product or operational confirmation.

## Key learnings

Retry policies that look similar operationally still need independent durable state when their limits and reset conditions differ. A single counter creates hidden coupling that can make one recovery path suppress another. Regression tests should cover both orderings whenever two bounded policies can interleave.

Tests for lock contention should synchronize on the event they are proving. A sleep can make the intended race likely, but it cannot guarantee the lock remains held under different runner load. An explicit release signal gives the test deterministic control of the critical section while leaving the production wait budget and lock behavior intact.

A green local test is useful diagnostic evidence but does not replace the configured remote check. The final handoff depends on the gate completing successfully against the checked branch tree, including remote validation.
